sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter is named (Y) /ɪ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (yes) /jɛs/, which expresses agreement. This letter makes four different sounds in English.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the middle of your tongue near the roof of your mouth. Let the voiced air flow smoothly over it. For the second sound, lift the tongue high and smile. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, then glide your tongue upward. For the fourth sound, drop your tongue slightly and relax your mouth. Put a hand on your throat to feel the voice buzz.

sections.title: Reading and spelling rules
paragraphs: At the start of a word or syllable before a vowel, this letter sounds like (yard) /jɑːd/. In an unstressed syllable at the end of a word, it sounds like (happy) /hæ.pi/. In an open stressed syllable or at the end of a one-beat word, it sounds like (my) /maɪ/. In a closed stressed syllable, it sounds like (myth) /mɪθ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not turn the first sound into an affricate like j in jam. An affricate is a consonant that starts as a plosive and ends as a fricative, like ch in chair. Keep your tongue from touching the roof of your mouth so the air glides through softly.
